articles.title_orig: Presidents Cup: Scottie Scheffler, Sam Burns sneak through tough opening round as U.S. takes early lead at Medinah
articles.title_zh: Presidents Cup: Scottie Scheffler, Sam Burns sneak through tough opening round as U.S. takes early lead at Medinah
articles.content_orig:
Nobody can legitimately question how good of a golfer Scottie Scheffler is. He's the top-ranked golfer in the world for a reason, and has absolutely dominated the PGA Tour over the last several years.
But Scheffler's struggles on the international stage, a trend he can't seem to shake, continued on Thursday at Medinah Country Club in Chicago.
Scheffler was in the opening group at the 2026 Presidents Cup on Thursday, playing alongside Sam Burns in the first of five four-ball matches against the International team. The two managed to sneak out a 1-up win over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, thanks to a huge save at the 17th, to get the United States on the board. It was also the first Presidents Cup or Ryder Cup match that Burns and Scheffler have won playing together.
By the end of the day, the U.S. took a 3-2 lead over the International team ahead of the foursomes matches on Friday. They've led after the opening session in 12 of the 16 Presidents Cups.
"We just did our best to stay in it," Scheffler said. "I felt like both teams got off to pretty hot starts today and we cooled off a little bit off that."
Scheffler opened the day with a walk-in birdie. But that was about his only highlight. Lee and Im quickly tied the match back up as Scheffler struggled to get much of anything going. He missed the green at the short par-3 7th and hit his tee shot into the crowd, for example, and couldn't get many putts to fall the rest of the way.
That largely left Burns as the one to try and hold things down. He sank a big birdie putt at the 9th to keep the match tied as they made the turn, and Lee and Im missed three straight birdie looks of their own that would have given them their first lead of the day. They finally jumped ahead of Burns and Scheffler on the 13th after Scheffler missed a 3-footer for birdie, though Burns made a putt on the 14th to even things up once again.
Scheffler got a 4-foot par putt to fall on the 17th, while Im missed a similar look in a rough mistake, to finally put the Americans in the lead for good. Scheffler had to save par after landing in the bunker at the 18th, however, to avoid splitting the point.
Scheffler's record on the international stage is lagging behind his other accomplishments. He's got a 3-6-3 record at the Ryder Cup, and he entered this week with a 3-5-1 record in Presidents Cup matches. Scheffler has never won a Presidents Cup singles match, either, though he's 2-0-1 in those at the Ryder Cup.
Scheffler and Burns, who are very good friends off the course, were a combined 0-3-1 when paired together at the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup before Thursday's win. Not great.
Luckily for Scheffler and the Americans, they're now in the lead after the first day in Chicago. Just not by much.
"I saw those guys competing their asses off out there," U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said. "I'm really proud of them. A session win is a session win, we're going to take it any way we can get it. So happy for Scottie and Sam to go out there in that lead match and get that big win for us to lead us off.
"This is a long week. This is one session. We've got four more to go. Just proud of the way these guys started us off."
While the Scheffler-Burns group was slow, two pairs of Americans wasted no time in their matches behind them.
Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun rolled to a 4&3 win over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria in the third match of the day. Koivun made three birdies on the front side to grab a lead almost immediately, and Koivun — who only made his PGA Tour debut mid-season earlier this year — looked comfortable out there.
Thomas then sank a birdie putt of his own from off the green at the 14th to push their lead back to three, which was enough to carry them to the early win. Thomas has now won his last seven four-ball matches at the Presidents Cup, which is tied for the all-time record. And at 21, Koivun is now the second-youngest American behind only Jordan Spieth to win a Presidents Cup match.
Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa cruised to a similar 3&2 win over Ryan Fox and Adam Scott. Clark went 4-under on the front nine himself, which was more than enough to keep Fox and Scott at bay. Clark then pushed their lead to three with a birdie on the 15th, which allowed them to end the match on the following hole.
Scott is playing in his 12th career Presidents Cup, and Thursday was his 55th overall match, both of which tied the all-time record with Phil Mickelson.
While they were in the last and slowest group of the day, Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim had little issue getting past Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay, winning 3&2 to secure an easy point for the Internationals.
They went 2-up through their first two holes to take control of the match almost instantly. While Cantlay and Gotterup rallied briefly — they made three birdies in a four-hole stretch to tie things up — that was all they could do. Cantlay became a non-factor the rest of the way while Kim and Kim easily pushed their lead to three before taking the win. Si Woo's birdie at the 14th was from distance, too, and banked in perfectly.
Tom nearly had a hole-in-one at the 16th and actually banked his ball off the flag stick. That would have been the third ace in Presidents Cup history.
Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune, meanwhile, took off on the back nine to grab their 3&1 win. After hanging in a battle on the front nine, the pair won back-to-back holes before making the turn to take control of the match while Xander Schauffele and Cameron Young struggled to get putts to fall. Eventually, after Young missed a birdie look at the 17th, Matsuyama and Hisatsune were able to put the Internationals on the board for the first time all day.
The two teams will return to Medinah on Friday for five foursomes, or alternate shot, matches.

Our second NFL week of the year is in the books, but unfortunately, it yielded multiple significant injuries, especially at the all-important quarterback position.
After a hot start to the year, New York Giants QB Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night, for which he will undergo season-ending knee surgery . Jameis Winston is set to start for the Giants for now, though head coach John Harbaugh did not rule out the potential for the team to trade for a veteran .
The Chicago Bears are also expected to be without their starting quarterback for now after Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury in Week 2. Head coach Ben Johnson dubbed him "week-to-week" on Monday , though the team did not yet officially rule him out for Week 3. That isn't the end of their quarterback woes, however, as backup Tyson Bagent was placed in the concussion protocol earlier this week, which could force the Bears to start QB3 Case Keenum against the Philadelphia Eagles this week.
Washington Commanders star Jayden Daniels also suffered a significant injury this week after dislocating his elbow for the second time since last season. He's already been ruled out for Week 3 and is expected to miss additional time, though it's unclear how much, as Daniels continues to gather opinions from specialists . Marcus Mariota will get the start in his absence.
One team that is getting past a bad injury is the Falcons. After two weeks of disappointing outings from Cooper Rush , Atlanta announced on Monday that Michael Penix Jr. will start for the Falcons on Thursday against the Packers . A healthy Tua Tagovailoa is reportedly set to back him up.
Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 3.
Starting Panthers receiver Jalen Coker might be trending the wrong way after suffering an ankle injury. Coker, who was limited in practice on Wednesday, did not practice with Carolina on Thursday.
During the media portion of Thursday's practice, WCNC's Nick Carboni captured Coker walking gingerly off the field.
The Panthers play the Browns on Sunday; at this rate, it seems less likely that Coker will be able to play.
Nick Chubb started his career as a Cleveland Brown, and he'll be ending it that way.
In an interview on ESPN Cleveland's Browns Daily, Haslam Sports Group managing partner JW Johnson announced the Chubb would be joining the team on Friday to officially retire as a Brown. Chubb will participate in a press conference, and will be present on Sunday as Cleveland hosts the Carolina Panthers.
"I'm just thrilled for Nick and proud of him and happy to call him a friend," Johnson said.
Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL in August, bringing his pro career to a somewhat early end. The running back played seven of his eight NFL seasons in Cleveland, spending last season with the Houston Texans.
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs remains on the NFL's commissioner exempt list . And in the lead-up to his team's Week 3 "Thursday Night Football" clash with the Atlanta Falcons , ESPN's Rob Demovsky reported the latest update involving the case that has sidelined Jacobs indefinitely.
In Wisconsin on Thursday, Brown County District Court Judge Marc A. Hammer denied the victim's request to permanently seal evidence, including the surveillance video the criminal complaint said captured a portion of the May 23 incident at Jacobs' home in Green Bay , as reported by ESPN .
Had the evidence been permanently sealed, the NFL might not have been able to review that video, which could affect the severity of punishment the league hands the three-time Pro Bowler.
The NFL's investigation into the matter is ongoing, and it could result in a suspension for Jacobs, although it's important to note that time served on the commissioner exempt list — which prevents a player from practicing with a team or playing in its games — would count toward a suspension. Jacobs has been on that list since Aug. 30 and, consequently, has missed the Packers' first two games of the 2026 campaign.
On Sept. 10, Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property . He was reportedly convicted of battery and fined $1,000. Additionally, per ESPN , the 28-year-old Jacobs accepted a deferred judgment agreement on the criminal damage to property charge.

The Ravens look like they will be without wide receiver Zay Flowers for a second straight week as they face the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro.
Flowers will not practice on Thursday as he deals with a hamstring injury. He was a limited participant in practice last week before being ruled out for Week 2.
There are 220 players with two or more catches this season. Among them: Nate Adkins, Jared Wayne, LaJohntay Wester, Brady Russell, Brevyn Spann-Ford and Lan Larison.
One notable player not on that list of 220: Marvin Harrison Jr.
It's early in the season but there is already a lot of worry about Harrison. It's not just two games. It's 31 largely underwhelming games into his career for the Arizona Cardinals receiver. He has just two 100-yard games. He has one game with more than six catches. And two games into this season he has one catch for 33 yards. The Cardinals threw it 28 times in Week 2 against the Seahawks and Harrison was targeted only once.
Harrison was one of the most exciting receiver prospects ever. He was the fourth overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft, after three really good quarterbacks (Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye) were picked. Nobody is excited anymore.
San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans did not practice Wednesday due to a hip injury, but it sounds like he'll be OK to play in Week 3, per NFL Network.
Evans' injury is said to be minor and he's expected to return to practice ahead of Week 3.
Evans proved he still had something left in the tank in Week 1, hauling in six catches and scoring a touchdown. He had more receiving yards in Week 2, but left the game early due to his injury. The 49ers were blowing out the Miami Dolphins at the time of the injury, however, so it's possible Evans could have kept playing in a more competitive game.
The Los Angeles Rams may not have Puka Nacua in Week 3. Head coach Sean McVay gave a pessimistic outlook on Nacua's recovery Thursday, saying the wideout is "not making great progress."
McVay made those comments during a radio appearance.
McVay added he has "a ton of confidence" in the remaining receivers if Nacua can't go.
The wideout is battling hip and groin issues and missed Week 2 due to those injuries. When healthy, Nacua is among the best receivers in the game.

By Wednesday, head coach John Harbaugh confirmed multiple reports that the decision was made: Jaxson Dart will undergo surgery to repair damage to his meniscus, MCL and PCL. His ACL is intact.
Harbaugh, whose appreciation for Dart strongly swayed his decision to join the Giants in January, is left to pick up the pieces of an offense now in the hands of Jameis Winston for the rest of the regular season (Harbaugh left open a potential postseason return for Dart).

Canadian authorities have confirmed a shooting near a synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, was a "hate-motivated" attack targeting the Jewish community.
The shooting took place outside the Sons of Jacob Synagogue on Sunday night during Yom Kippur, the holiest night in the Jewish calendar.
Belleville police chief Murray Rodd said during a Thursday news conference that it was "a deliberate attack directed at members of the Jewish community".
A police officer who was critically injured in the incident continued to fend off the attacker despite being shot multiple times, the police chief said.
The officer, identified as Constable Jeff Smith, suffered multiple gunshot wounds to his head and body, Rodd said. Smith remains in hospital and is expected to undergo multiple surgeries related to "serious head trauma".
"He's making progress every day," the chief said.
Smith was shot in his car but sought to fend off the attack on the synagogue until a second officer arrived almost three minutes later.
"Despite suffering life-threatening injuries, within moments of encountering the armed suspect, Constable Smith exited his vehicle and engaged the attacker," Rodd said.
The second officer, Constable Mike McCurdy, "joined the active gunfight, helping to bring the violent attack to an end", the police chief said. McCrudy was not injured.
Both officers discharged their firearms, authorities said earlier this week.
Around 20 to 30 shots were fired, leaving the suspect in life-threatening condition and Smith in critical but stable condition.
The gunman was identified by police as 29-year-old Sean Ward from Quinte West, a community near Belleville and about 170km (105 miles) east of Toronto. He was sent to hospital with serious injuries and later died.
Rodd called the attempted attack a "hate-motivated crime".
Toronto police have increased patrols outside synagogues and places of worship out of an abundance of caution.
Leaders of the Jewish community, as well as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and other politicians, condemned antisemitic violence in the aftermath of the incident.
Noah Shack, CEO of the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs, said in a statement on Thursday that "if not for the extraordinary bravery of Constable Jeff Smith, Canadians would have experienced the type of mass-casualty terror attack our security services have warned is a realistic possibility".
He called on Canadian leaders to "take urgent and concrete actions" against threats toward the Jewish community.
Carney wrote on X earlier this week that "Jewish people must be able to worship safely. To live free, open, proud Jewish lives."
